explanation.title: Shortest Collaboration Path
explanation.graphNotes: Neo4j provides native shortestPath() using bidirectional breadth-first search directly over physical graph pointers, terminating immediately upon meeting.
explanation.relationalNotes: Oracle SQL requires a recursive CTE constructing path strings, tracking search depth, and pruning cycles with a CYCLE clause or string pattern check, ordered by depth ASC.
explanation.whyGraph: Shortest path is a core graph primitive natively executed inside Neo4j's traversal engine. In relational SQL, simulating graph BFS requires recursive CTE evaluation with string concatenation.

oracle.query:
WITH coauthor_rel (a1, a2, paper_id) AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT pa1.AuthorID, pa2.AuthorID, pa1.PaperID
  FROM PAPER_AUTHOR pa1
  JOIN PAPER_AUTHOR pa2 ON pa1.PaperID = pa2.PaperID
  WHERE pa1.AuthorID <> pa2.AuthorID
),
path_search (current_author, path_str, depth) AS (
  SELECT a2, TO_CHAR(:fromAuthorId || '->' || paper_id || '->' || a2), 1
  FROM coauthor_rel
  WHERE a1 = :fromAuthorId
  UNION ALL
  SELECT r.a2, TO_CHAR(ps.path_str || '->' || r.paper_id || '->' || r.a2), ps.depth + 1
  FROM path_search ps
  JOIN coauthor_rel r ON ps.current_author = r.a1
  WHERE ps.depth < 4
)
CYCLE current_author SET is_cycle TO 'Y' DEFAULT 'N'
SELECT depth AS hops, path_str
FROM path_search
WHERE current_author = :toAuthorId
ORDER BY depth ASC
FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY

neo4j.query:
MATCH (a1:Author {authorId: $fromAuthorId}), (a2:Author {authorId: $toAuthorId})
OPTIONAL MATCH p = shortestPath((a1)-[:WROTE*..8]-(a2))
RETURN toInteger(length(p) / 2) AS hops, [n IN nodes(p) | coalesce(n.name, n.title)] AS path_nodes
